doc_name: List of In Living Color cast members
text: During the five-season run of In Living Color (Fox-TV, 1990–1994), cast members frequently changed, though some earlier members continued into later seasons, meaning later casts included individuals from previous years. Jim Carrey, Tommy Davidson, David Alan Grier, and T'Keyah Crystal Keymáh were the only cast members present for all five seasons. Chris Rock was never an official cast member but appeared as a "special guest star" in several skits during the fifth season, reprising his "Cheap Pete" character from I'm Gonna Git You Sucka. In the early years, Rock was parodied as the sole African American cast member on Saturday Night Live, despite SNL also having Tim Meadows and Ellen Cleghorne; in an SNL Mother's Day skit, Rock’s mother jokes that she is disappointed in him for being on SNL and asks, "Has In Living Color called yet?" and later, when Adam Sandler hosted, Chris Rock sang about being fired from SNL and kicked off In Living Color when the latter show was canceled. Other recurring guest stars in the fifth season included writer Nick Bakay (in The Dirty Dozens sketches) and Peter Marshall (as ringmaster for urban parodies of Hollywood Squares), as well as rapper Biz Markie, who appeared in various roles such as Wanda the Ugly Woman’s sister in drag or as "Dirty Dozens" contestant Damian "Foosball" Franklin. The Fly Girls troupe had multiple members throughout the show’s run; the original lineup was Cari French, Carrie Ann Inaba, Deidre Lang, Lisa Marie Todd, and Michelle Whitney-Morrison. Rosie Perez served as choreographer for the first four seasons, with Deidre Lang being the only Fly Girl to stay for the entire run. The Fly Girls were sometimes used as extras or in opening gags—such as a sketch where they performed open-heart surgery, revealing they were dancing to pay for medical school—but mostly appeared in commercial break bumpers and filler scenes between sketches, similar to the bikini-clad female cast members on Rowan and Martin's Laugh-In. In the fifth season, Arthur Rainer became the main choreographer, with Lisa Joann Thompson and Deidre Lang as assistant choreographers.
